description: The pie chart represents the distribution of difficulty across a dataset, comparing the proportions of different difficulty levels. The chart is divided into five slices, representing the categories "Medium", "Hard", "Easy", "Very hard", and "Very easy". The slices are colored red, blue, green, orange, and purple, respectively. The proportions are approximately 51.8% for "Medium", 25.7% for "Hard", 11.2% for "Easy", 6.5% for "Very hard", and 4.7% for "Very easy". The chart includes a legend that maps the colors to their corresponding categories, and percentage labels are shown for some of the slices. The slices appear to be ordered in descending size, with "Medium" being the largest and "Very easy" being the smallest. The chart is labeled "Distribution of Difficulty" at the bottom.
